A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same Toeplitz framework, synthetic tasks and deposit-pattern investigation. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic-task learning curves, head-ablation experiments and numerical comparisons of MLA, RoPE and NoPE.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds positional-vector ablations, depth comparisons and reported multi-trigger generalization experiments.

M1.justification: The existing PE configurations, partial RoPE, Absolute+RoPE and MLA procedures are retained. Expanded theoretical analysis and simplified MLA equations do not establish an implemented change to the underlying algorithms.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix E reports an additional family of multi-trigger tasks requiring combinations of pairwise distances, evaluated beyond training length. This extends the original pairwise-distance and counting coverage to compositional positional reasoning and length shifts, although results are documented only qualitatively.

E2.justification: The six main comparators remain Absolute, Relative/T5, ALiBi, NoPE, RoPE and Random embeddings. Table 1 retains the same MLA/RoPE/NoPE comparison. Newly introduced random-vector interventions are ablation controls rather than additional PE comparison methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds an eight-layer configuration, norm-matched random-vector controls and testing beyond training length. Task 1 labels are now described as binned distances rather than absolute index distances. Original splits, model widths and training budgets remain; rerunning the retained results is not established.

E4.justification: New Section 5.4 tests where positional information resides by removing positional vectors versus matched random vectors. Appendix D.2 adds depth robustness evidence, and Appendix E investigates compositional generalization failure. Earlier hybrid, partial-RoPE and MLA ablations remain present.

E5.justification: V1 lists seed 42 without an uncertainty summary. V2 reports five-seed averages, lists seeds 0, 42, 70, 113 and 130, and states variance below 5%. Figure 8 also displays random-control means and ±1σ bands.

E6.justification: V2 adds positional-vector ablation results, complete head profiles including an eight-layer model, and qualitative multi-trigger extrapolation failures. Original performance graphics and Table 1 values remain unchanged, including MLA's 88.34/97.41 and RoPE's 92.64/69.43 on Tasks 1/2. These are added findings, not demonstrated improvements under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: New Section 6 and Appendix C introduce Jacobian and gradient assumptions, softmax-gradient lemmas, RoPE seed and ALiBi cancellation propositions, and an exponential-specialization theorem with proofs. Earlier spectral arguments remain, partly relocated. The Toeplitz assumption is also recast in terms of a positional Gram matrix.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds spectral contraction, optimization benefits and predicted specialization. V2 makes RoPE's performance paradox and an allegedly intrinsic training bias central contributions, claiming a gradient-based proof that its architecture produces single-head concentration.

C2.justification: V2 develops interpretations of deposit as training-induced collapse rather than reusable modularity, positional information shifting from activations into query–key parameters, and frequency concentration causing massive values. Multi-trigger failures support a new compositionality argument. Direct validation of the proposed link to length-generalization difficulties remains acknowledged as outstanding.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository URL and more specific vocabulary and trigger-count descriptions. Most implementation settings and the RTX 4090 disclosure are retained. Documentation remains inconsistent: the main text specifies 1,000 vocabulary tokens while Tables 3–4 still specify 574; new multi-trigger tests lack detailed settings.

R1.justification: Related work is largely retained. V2 adds the Dosovitskiy et al. vision-Transformer citation and expands connections to previously cited work on latent positional representations, frequency training and massive values. Bibliographic restyling alone does not represent additional literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial methodological and experimental prose are rewritten. Ablations are reorganized into hypothesis/design/results subsections, head specialization moves into Section 4, spectral material moves into Appendix B, and a new theoretical section and proof appendix restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned with additional labels and legends; Figure 8 and full head-ablation grids in Figures 9–10 are added. Existing figures receive expanded captions, reordered placement and renumbering within a revised conference layout. Original performance graphics, comparison tables and partial-RoPE appendix plots are retained.

improvement.justification: New controls, depth results, seed reporting and code information improve transparency. However, stronger conclusions conflict with displayed evidence: Figure 6 calls one head nearly optimal despite roughly 0.52 accuracy versus 0.93 with all heads, and Figure 9 shows a substantial Layer-2 ablation loss despite describing other heads' effects as minor. Appendix C.5 also does not establish the greater-than-one gains required by the new amplification theorem. These benefits and evidential problems prevent a reliable net improvement judgment.
